name: Combobox

examples.title: A Searchable Select
examples.code:
<form onSubmit={e => e.preventDefault()}>
  <Combobox
    label="Country"
    placeholder="Pick a country"
    data={['Canada', 'France', 'Germany', 'Japan', 'Kenya', 'Mexico']}
    empty="No countries match"
  />
  <Input label="City" />
  <Input label="Postal code" />
  <Button type="submit" color="primary">
    Save address
  </Button>
</form>

examples.title: Groups
examples.code:
<form onSubmit={e => e.preventDefault()}>
  <Combobox
    label="Produce"
    keepFirst
    data={[
      { value: 'Apple', group: 'Fruit' },
      { value: 'Banana', group: 'Fruit' },
      { value: 'Cherry', group: 'Fruit' },
      { value: 'Carrot', group: 'Vegetables' },
      { value: 'Leek', group: 'Vegetables' },
      { value: 'Pea', group: 'Vegetables' },
    ]}
  />
  <Input label="Quantity" type="number" min={1} defaultValue={1} />
  <Input label="Deliver on" type="date" />
  <Input label="Note for the shopper" />
  <Button type="submit" color="primary">
    Add to order
  </Button>
</form>

examples.title: Disabled Items
examples.code:
<form onSubmit={e => e.preventDefault()}>
  <Combobox
    label="Delivery"
    defaultValue="standard"
    data={[
      { value: 'standard', label: 'Standard, in 3 to 5 days' },
      { value: 'express', label: 'Express, next day' },
      { value: 'pickup', label: 'Pick up in store', disabled: true },
    ]}
  />
  <Input label="Note for the courier" />
  <Button type="submit" color="primary">
    Place order
  </Button>
</form>

examples.title: Several Values, with Tags
examples.code:
<form onSubmit={e => e.preventDefault()}>
  <Combobox
    label="Labels"
    multiple
    placeholder="Find a label"
    defaultValue={['docs']}
    data={['bug', 'docs', 'feature', 'question']}
  />

    <option>Low</option>
    <option>Medium</option>
    <option>High</option>
  </Select>
  <Button type="submit" color="primary">
    Save issue
  </Button>
</form>

examples.title: Where the List Opens
examples.code:
<Modal active={active} onClose={close} aria-label="Edit shipping">
  <Modal.Background onClick={close} />
  <Modal.Card>
    <Modal.Card.Body>
      <ConfigProvider portalContainer={overlay ?? undefined}>
        <Combobox
          label="Country"
          data={countries}
          appendToBody
          position="auto"
        />
      </ConfigProvider>
    </Modal.Card.Body>
  </Modal.Card>
  {/* In the modal and outside the card, so the card can't clip it. */}
  <div ref={setOverlay} />
</Modal>

accessibility:
- **The roles:** the field is `role="combobox"` with `aria-autocomplete="list"` and
  `aria-haspopup="listbox"`. The list is a `listbox` of `option`s, and a group is a `group` named by
  its heading. This is the ARIA 1.2 combobox the ARIA Authoring Practices describe.
- **Focus stays in the field:** the highlighted item is the field's `aria-activedescendant`.
  When a key or the list opening moves the highlight, the item is scrolled into view, since a
  browser only scrolls to what has focus. The pointer moves it without scrolling, since the pointer
  is already on that item. A click on an item keeps focus in the field too.
- **`aria-expanded`** is `true` while a list with an item in it is on screen, and
  `aria-controls` points at the list then. While the menu shows just the empty message, the
  field says it's collapsed, and so does the server markup for a list rendered with
  `appendToBody`, which shows only once the page has hydrated.
- **The list's name** comes from the label that names the field: the Combobox's `label`, or an
  outer `Field`'s. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you put on `Combobox.List` wins, and
  with none of these the list is named "Suggestions". Given `data`, an `aria-label` or
  `aria-labelledby` on the Combobox names the field and the list, so it needs no `label`.
- **`aria-selected`, with one value,** is on the highlighted item and nothing else, the way the
  Authoring Practices' combobox examples do it. The value shows as a check mark, which doesn't rely
  on color, and the list opens with the highlight on it. Several libraries put `aria-selected` on
  the chosen item instead.
- **With `multiple`,** the list is `aria-multiselectable`, and each item's `aria-selected` is its
  `checked`.
- **Disabled items** are `aria-disabled` and stay reachable with the arrows, the Authoring
  Practices' advice for listbox options, so a screen reader user finds them. They're never picked
  or `aria-selected`, and the opening highlight and `keepFirst` pass over them.
- **The empty message** sits beside the list, not in it, so it isn't counted as an item. When
  your typing brings it on screen, its text is announced through a polite status region that's in
  the page from the start, once each time the matches run out. Opening the list with it already
  there, or emptying the field, announces nothing. While `isLoading` is on, or a loading `Control`
  is around the Combobox, the announcement waits and is made once loading ends. In a menu,
  keep it to text: Tab closes the list before a keyboard user can reach a link or a button in it.
  An `inline` list stays on screen, so a link or a button beside it is in the Tab order.
- **Tags,** with `multiple` and `data`: the field's `aria-describedby` points at the tags' labels,
  since its own text is the search, so focusing it reads the picks. Each tag's button is named
  "Remove" and the item's label, or `ariaCloseLabel` with the label as its description, and
  taking a tag off puts focus back in the field, which then reads the picks that are left.
- **No counts are announced,** for the reasons in [A Result Count](https://bestax.io/docs/api/form/combobox#a-result-count).
- **Enter and Escape:** Enter submits the form when nothing is highlighted, and Escape only stops
  at the Combobox when it closed a panel that was on screen.
- **Forced colors:** in Windows high contrast mode the highlight is drawn as an outline in the
  system's highlight color, a disabled item takes the system's color for disabled text, and the
  check mark and the panel's edge stay visible.
summary: The `Combobox` component is a text field with a list to pick from under it, for a searchable select, a multi-select with tags, grouped items or a server search: given `data` it does the rest, and built from parts it leaves the data to you. Given `data`, it's one element. It renders the field, the menu, the list, the groups and the empty message, filters the items by label as the user types, and keeps the value, which `onChange` reports. With `multiple`, the picks show as tags under the field. Built from parts, the app owns the data: what's in the list, how it's filtered, and the value. A pick calls `onSelect` with the item's `value`, and the Combobox keeps no value and never changes the text in the field, so the app sets both there. Nothing filters the items either, so a server's answer shows as it came. For a free-text field with suggestions, `Autocomplete` is the simpler choice. Either way, focus stays in the field, and the highlighted item is its `aria-activedescendant`. With one value, the highlighted item is the `aria-selected` one, as the ARIA Authoring Practices' combobox does it, and a `checked` item shows a check mark and takes the highlight when the list opens. With `multiple`, `checked` is each item's `aria-selected`. Tab and focus leaving close the menu without picking. When typing leaves the empty message on screen, its text is announced through a polite status region, once, after any loading ends. Result counts aren't announced: a screen reader reads the list's size from the markup, and a count on every keystroke talks over the typing. Show one in a `role="status"` line beside the field when it matters.

props.name: data
props.description: The items, for a Combobox that renders the field, the menu, the list, the groups and the empty message itself. A string is an item whose label is its value, and an object is `{ value, label?, disabled?, group? }`. Typing filters the items by label, ignoring case, and the Combobox keeps the value. Leave it out to build the Combobox from parts.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several values can be picked. The list stays open after a pick, it's `aria-multiselectable`, and each item's `checked` is its `aria-selected`. With `data`, the value is an array, and the picks show as tags under the field, inside its Field, each with a button that takes it off. The field's description lists them, since its text is the search.

props.name: value
props.description: The value, controlled, with `data`: the picked item's `value`, or `null` for none, and with `multiple` an array of them. With one value, the field shows the picked item's label while you aren't typing in it, and the list closing or the field being left puts it back over any typing. A field emptied and left like that clears the value.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value to start with when uncontrolled, with `data`.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new value, with `data`, when a pick, a tag's button or a field left empty changes it: an item's `value` or `null`, or with `multiple` the array.

props.name: ariaCloseLabel
props.description: Names each tag's button, in place of "Remove" and the item's label, as Taginput's does. The button is then described by its tag's label, so it still says which tag it takes off.

props.name: children
props.description: The parts, in order: `Combobox.Input`, then `Combobox.Menu` with `Combobox.List` and `Combobox.Empty` in it. With `inline`, the `Combobox.List` and `Combobox.Empty` go straight in. Render `Combobox.List` while there are items and `Combobox.Empty` while there aren't: the empty message sits beside the list, not in it. With `data` there are none to give: children given with it are ignored, with a warning in development.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The field's placeholder, with `data`.

props.name: name
props.description: A form field name, with `data`. A hidden input posts the value, empty while there's none, and with `multiple` a hidden input posts each value.

props.name: empty
props.description: What the menu shows in place of the list, with `data`, when nothing matches the typing, such as "No countries match". It's announced the way `Combobox.Empty` is. Without it, the menu closes while nothing matches.

props.name: itemTemplate
props.description: Renders an item's content, with `data`, in place of its label. It's handed the item from `data`, a string there arriving as `{ value, label }`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: The field can't be used, with `data`: it can't be focused or typed in, its items can't be picked, its tags lose their buttons, and its hidden inputs don't post, the way a disabled field's value doesn't.

props.name: required
props.description: A value is needed, with `data`. The field is `required` while nothing is picked, so the browser's own check stops the form the way it does for Autocomplete's field, and it's `aria-required` the whole time. The check reads the field's text, which the list closing, Enter's included, puts back to the pick. An `inline` list never closes, so there it's leaving the field that does.

props.name: form
props.description: The id of the form the value posts with, with `data`, for a field outside it. It goes on the hidden inputs, and on the field so that form checks `required` too.

props.name: id
props.description: The field's `id`, with `data`, which the label then points at, and so can a label of your own. Built from parts, it lands on `div.combobox`, so give `Combobox.Input` the `id` instead.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the field and the list, with `data`, in place of a `label`. Built from parts, it lands on `div.combobox`, so put it on `Combobox.Input`.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The ids of what names the field and the list, with `data`, in place of a `label`. Built from parts, it lands on `div.combobox`, so put it on `Combobox.Input`.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's label, which names `Combobox.Input` through `htmlFor`, and the list through `aria-labelledby`. Dropped inside an outer `Field`, whose label names both instead when it points at the field. When `Combobox.Input` has an `id` of its own, server markup names the field through `aria-labelledby` until the page hydrates and the label's `for` catches up.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Props for the label element. An explicit `htmlFor` takes over the association: give `Combobox.Input` the same `id`, and the list is still named after the label.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. When set, opening and closing only report through `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the open state asked for: `true` from typing, a click in the field or Down Arrow, and `false` from Escape, Tab, a pick with one value, focus leaving or a press outside. Fires in controlled and uncontrolled use.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with an item's `value` when it's picked with Enter or a click. A disabled item is never picked. With `data`, `onChange` reports the value that follows. Built from parts, the Combobox keeps no value and doesn't change the text in the field: update yours here.

props.name: keepFirst
props.description: Highlights the first enabled item whenever the list opens or its items change, so Enter picks the top match. It only highlights: leaving the field still picks nothing, and so does Tab.

props.name: inline
props.description: The list is always on screen, in the flow under the field, as in a Popover or a page panel. There's no menu, so nothing closes it, and Escape goes to whatever is around it.

props.name: position
props.description: Where the menu opens against the field: below (`bottom-*`) or above (`top-*`), lined up with its left or right edge. `auto` picks the one that keeps the list in the viewport, preferring below. The same union Popover takes.

props.name: appendToBody
props.description: Renders the menu through `Portal`, into the `portalContainer` a `ConfigProvider` sets, `document.body` by default, fixed to the viewport at the field, so a container that clips its overflow can't cut it off. It then shows from the commit after hydration, never in server markup. Theming variables set on an ancestor reach it only when the portal's container is inside that ancestor, as with Popover. In a `Modal`, point `portalContainer` inside the modal, so the list stays in the dialog for assistive tech.

props.name: size
props.description: Sizes the field and the items together.

props.name: labelSize
props.description: Size for the label (used in horizontal layouts).

props.name: horizontal
props.description: Horizontal field layout.

props.name: message
props.description: Help/validation message below the input.

props.name: messageColor
props.description: Bulma color for the message.

props.name: fieldClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Field wrapper.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the `div.combobox` around the field and the list.

parts.summary: The text field, with the combobox role and the keys, rendered as an `Input`.

props.name: iconLeft
props.description: Icon props for left icon. Bulma gives control icons `pointer-events: none`, so a clickable node here never receives a click. Put a button beside the input in its own addon `Control` instead.

props.name: iconRight
props.description: Icon props for right icon. Bulma gives control icons `pointer-events: none`, so a clickable node here never receives a click. Put a button beside the input in its own addon `Control` instead.

props.name: iconLeftName
props.description: Shortcut for left icon name.

props.name: iconRightName
props.description: Shortcut for right icon name.

props.name: iconLeftSize
props.description: Shortcut for left icon size.

props.name: iconRightSize
props.description: Shortcut for right icon size.

props.name: hasIconsLeft
props.description: Force left icon container.

props.name: hasIconsRight
props.description: Force right icon container.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner on the `Control` it renders. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the spinner stops and stays drawn (with bestax's CSS loaded). The spinner sits at the right edge, where `iconRight` also sits, and the two overlap; leave the right icon out while loading.

props.name: isExpanded
props.description: Expand the control.

props.name: controlSize
props.description: Control size.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Control.

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color modifier for the input.

props.name: isRounded
props.description: Rounded input corners.

props.name: isStatic
props.description: Styles the input as static text. It stays editable; add `readOnly` to stop edits.

props.name: isHovered
props.description: Applies hovered state.

props.name: isFocused
props.description: Applies focused state.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes to apply.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disabled input.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Read-only input.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the underlying element.

parts.catchAll: All standard <input> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: The floating panel under the field, on screen while the list is open and its children aren't all empty.

props.name: children
props.description: What the panel shows: `Combobox.List` while there are items, and `Combobox.Empty` while there aren't. Children that are all `null`, `false` or `''`, or empty Fragments, keep the panel shut, so write the conditional here. A component that renders nothing, or a `Combobox.List` with no items in it, still counts, and shows an empty panel.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

parts.summary: The list of items, a `listbox` named by the label that names the field.

props.name: children
props.description: `Combobox.Item`s and `Combobox.Group`s, in the order they're shown.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

parts.summary: One choice in the list, with a check mark while it's `checked`.

props.name: value
props.description: What `onSelect` hands back. Unique within the Combobox.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Can't be picked. The arrows still reach it, so a screen reader user finds it, and it's never `aria-selected`.

props.name: checked
props.description: It's the value, or one of them. It shows a check mark, the list opens with the highlight on it, and with `multiple` it's the `aria-selected`.

props.name: children
props.description: What the item shows: text, or text with an avatar, a tag or a hint.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

parts.summary: Items under a heading, a `group` named by it.

props.name: label
props.description: The heading, which also names the group for assistive tech, unless you give the group an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` of its own.

props.name: children
props.description: The group's `Combobox.Item`s.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

parts.summary: The message shown in place of the list when nothing matches, announced when typing brings it on screen.

props.name: children
props.description: The message, such as "No countries match". Its text is announced when typing brings it on screen and isn't read again while it stays, so a message that names the query is heard for the first query only.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.
